doc.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

chapter: Making A Great Day in Harlem
title: Tracking down people in the photo: the boy by Basie and Willie the Lion
summary: She found the boy through an Amsterdam News ad; Basie sat down and Willie the Lion Smith wandered off.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well I found him, because I put an ad in the Amsterdam News which is a Harlem newspaper, with the photograph. See I loved all this part of producing the movie, tracking people down, loved that. And I said, “do you remember this photo?” I said, “it ran in Esquire” and I told the date and it was taken in the summer of ‘58. “Were you there? Do you know anyone who was? If so call this number.” And I had a separate telephone with © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-

an answering machine attached. And people started checking in. And one was the little boy sitting next to Basie. So that was nice. Basie sat down when everybody else was standing, because I think his legs gave out. And in later years of course he was in this wheelchair that he drove himself. It was kind of marvelous. But the other person that decided to sit down was Willie the Lion Smith. And he’s so big and pompous and arrogant you know. And he was standing there with this man who is half his size, Lucky Roberts had his arm around him and then in the last picture, he wanders off to the steps of the brownstone, just out of the frame, so he didn’t get in the picture in Esquire. He must have been kicking himself. Too bad. But he’s in the home movies that Mona Hinton shot that I’ve used in my movies. So you see him, you know, standing, very pompous and cute.
There’s two marvelous people, for you, Milt and Mona.
